The Philippine Eagle 
(Pithecophaga jefferyi) 

Also known as the monkey-eating eagle, it is one of the largest and rarest raptors in the world. Endemic to the Philippine rainforests, this critically endangered apex predator requires massive, undisturbed tracts of mature, old-growth canopy forest to hunt and nest successfully. The species has been pushed close to extinction by deforestation, severe habitat fragmentation, and hunting and trapping. Because each breeding pair requires an estimated 25 to 50 square miles of forest to survive, the Mabaka tribe’s expansion of their community-patrolled sanctuary directly preserves the unfragmented canopy these birds of prey need.
